newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares end mixed in speculative trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares end mixed in speculative trade.

text.p: Shares ended mixed in speculation driven trade at the Nigerian stock market on Thursday, traders said.
The all-share index closed at 6,910.30 from 6,892.19 on Wednesday.
Activity was slow as traders said business had begun to wind down for the year.
The recent turnaround in brewing shares persisted, seeing Nigerian Breweries and Guinness rise 30 kobo apiece to 18.50 naira and 7.70 naira respectively.
Strong interest in Nestle Foods saw the shares rise 1.00 naira to 47.00 naira.
African Petroleum and Total led oil marketing shares, gaining 40 kobo each to close at 43.20 naira and 56.00 naira respectively. National Oil rose 37 kobo to 44.87 naira.
Other strong finishers on Thursday were West African Portland Cement which at 43.00 naira rose by 45 kobo and Okomu Oil Palm which was 20 kobo up at 7.90 naira on recent good performances.
Bank and conglomerate shares fell due to lack of buyers.
Union Bank closed down 25 kobo at 5.05 naira, while Afribank ended at 4.10 naira, down 20 kobo.
UAC closed 20 kobo lower at 7.40 naira while Lever Brothers and CFAO slipped 10 kobo to 21.50 naira and 2.90 naira respectively.
There was a resurgence of interest in government stocks on Thursday.

One deal was for 3.1 million units at 95.97 naira of paper with a 12.50 percent coupon rate expiring in 2011. The other was for 5,000 units at 96.04 naira of a paper with a 12.50 percent coupon rate with a 14-year tenure.
